did: HOST1 laid the foundation for the essays' living cast. First the outward reach: Rive, Lottie and Spine were each ruled out for a stated reason, so we build only the gap over the SVG rig the owner chose. Then the closed unions every scene picks from, keyed by character, so Tin Bird can't be given Mochi's own beats: nine shared emotions, Mochi's five own beats, the NFL celebration as Mochi's ceremony, three shots and five placements. They live beside the cast so the phone can read them, with a seeded idle (blink, breath, glance, the key's turn) that gives the same picture for the same moment. The video draws them as a new burn-in kind that floats over the card. A cut list placing the host rendered twice to the same bytes.

calls.title: Where the host's unions and rig live
options: Beside the cast, in @some-ui/styles/brand/host, with the burn-ins host kind wrapping them
In burn-ins, as the issue first said
A new workspace for the cast's motion
calls.why: The Cast wing and the signature run on the phone and need the unions and the drawing, and burn-ins is a web-only workspace. The coordinator agreed (C1521).
calls.undo: Move brand/host.ts into burn-ins and import it from there; the phone would then need a copy.

calls.title: The first members of the host's unions
options: The owner's six emotions plus neutral, curious and taciturn; Mochi's five own beats; ceremonies keyed by character; one beat on screen per host burn-in
Only the owner's six emotions and Mochi's beats
One host burn-in drawing both characters at once
calls.why: A conversation spends most of its time in quiet states the owner named (taciturn, curious), and keying ceremonies by character lets the type refuse an NFL celebration on Tin Bird (C1522).
calls.undo: Edit the lists in packages/some-styles/src/brand/host.ts; the compiler then asks for each drawing.

left: HOST3 and HOST4: each emotion's and ceremony's drawing is a stub in EMOTION_DRAWINGS or CEREMONY_DRAWINGS in packages/some-styles/src/brand/host.ts. Fill an entry with a Redraw(nodes, tMs) that moves named data-part nodes, as the idle moves eyes and key. Tin Bird's lids, wings and lower beak aren't parts yet; the claude/host-ab prototype's gen.ts adds them.
HOST3 and HOST4: a new moving part needs a data-part name in cast.ts, and the cast's text then changes for every page drawing it (thumbnails included), though not their pictures.

HOST8 and HOST16: import the unions and hostAt from @some-ui/styles/brand/host, never from burn-ins. hostAt(beats, seed, t, area) gives the box, opacity and SVG over any area; a preview can draw the SVG as an img data URL, as the burn-ins stage does.
The cut list's zod schema in packages/ui/burn-ins/src/lib/host.ts is held to the unions by a test, not the compiler, so a new member needs no schema edit, but a new character needs a branch there.

motion video can't draw any burn-in yet; the host renders through pnpm --filter www record:short (set PLAYWRIGHT_CHROMIUM_EXECUTABLE_PATH=/opt/pw-browsers/chromium in a cloud session). Giving motion video a recorder is a possible later story.
Speaking motion is HOST5's: a beat's speaking flag reaches the frame but draws nothing yet.
The Rust Rounds note-cap test flaked on #3559's CI; filed as #3560.
